question:
A 6-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her father for her annual check-up. The father
describes her as a happy and healthy child but occasionally expresses concern about her weight. He
notes that she is a “picky” eater, preferring chicken nuggets and French fries. He has also observed
mild acne on her cheeks and forehead, attributing it to her dislike of bathing. The father states that she
has met all developmental milestones, recently started kindergarten, can tell time, and is beginning to
read. Her teacher reports that she interacts well with classmates. The patient was born at 38 weeks
gestation, has no chronic medical conditions, and takes a multivitamin. Her height and weight are
above the 95th percentile. Vital signs include a temperature of 98.7°F (37°C), blood pressure of 128/78
mmHg, pulse of 101/min, respirations of 14/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. On
physical examination, scattered comedones are observed on her forehead and cheeks. Bilateral
palpable breast tissue with raised and enlarged areolae is present. She also has scant axillary hair and

coarse pubic hair. A left-hand radiograph reveals a bone age of 9 years. Her serum follicular
stimulating hormone (FSH) level is 9.6 mU/mL (normal range 0.7-5.3 mU/mL), and luteinizing hormone
(LH) level is 6.4 mU/mL (normal range < 0.26 mU/mL). What is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
Answer Choices: (A) Karyotype analysis (B) Thyroid function tests (C) Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate
levels (D) Bone marrow biopsy (E) Serum testosterone levels (F) 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels (G)
Head computed tomography (CT) (H) Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain (I) Pelvic
ultrasound (J) Serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels
 A. Thyroid function tests
B. Serum testosterone levels
C. Serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels
D. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain
E. Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate levels
F. 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels
G. Head computed tomography (CT)
H. Karyotype analysis
I. Bone marrow biopsy
J. Pelvic ultrasound
